item.title: China's AI reality goes beyond market volatility
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-28
China's AI reality goes beyond market volatility BEIJING, Nov. 27 (Xinhua) -- As valuations across the global artificial intelligence (AI) industry come under renewed scrutiny, China's AI sector has also experienced market swings, prompting questions about its growth prospects, with some even warning of a bubble on the verge of bursting. Yet such assessments risk conflating market volatility with the long-term trajectory of an entire industry, while overlooking a more fundamental question: Is meaningful progress of an industry defined by financial investment returns, or by technological advances and its ability to address real-world needs? Evidence from China's AI sector points to an industry with tangible momentum. In 2025, China's core AI industries were valued at over 1.2 trillion yuan (about 179 billion U.S. dollars), up 40 percent year on year, with the number of AI enterprises exceeding 6,200, according to industry authorities. More importantly, AI in China is moving rapidly out of the lab, to factory floors, logistics networks, power grids and hospitals. Official data showed that more than 30 percent of large industrial enterprises in China have adopted AI, and leading smart factories have embedded the technology in over 70 percent of their operations. While investors tend to focus on balance sheets, Chinese industries are looking at broader productivity gains. A September study by the International Labour Organization on AI adoption in Chinese enterprises found efficiency gains of 30 to 100 percent across core workflows. In smart manufacturing, production efficiency improvements reached 20 to 30 percent. The global uptake of Chinese AI models speaks to the sector's technological progress. On OpenRouter, a leading global AI platform, Chinese AI models recorded 119.1 trillion tokens in weekly usage between Nov. 9 and 15, ranking first worldwide for the 29th consecutive week. The open-source approach of Chinese models has offered cost-effective solutions for businesses worldwide. These advances have come despite an increasingly restrictive external environment. Expanding technology controls from the West have constrained Chinese firms' access to advanced AI chips, semiconductor manufacturing equipment and related technologies. It highlights an inherent contradiction: If China's AI industry were merely a speculative bubble, what would explain the sustained efforts to contain its development as a strategic threat? External restrictions may raise costs, but are unlikely to derail China's AI development. While it still has considerable ground to make up in advanced AI chips and computing infrastructure, the country has laid out a clear strategic roadmap that makes AI a priority in its long-term development. In its 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), China has called for breakthroughs in core AI technologies and the full implementation of the "AI Plus" initiative, which aims to integrate AI into technological innovation, industrial development and a wide range of economic and social activities. China is also well placed to turn these ambitions into reality. Backed by a vast domestic market, a dynamic industrial ecosystem, solid infrastructure and diverse application scenarios, the country is aiming to bring the scale of AI-related industries to over 10 trillion yuan by the end of 2030. China's vast power supply gives its AI industry another solid foundation for scaling up, as the country generates about one-third of the world's electricity and has built the world's largest and fastest-growing renewable energy system. The country has also been accelerating efforts to expand its computing capacity. Data from the National Data Administration showed that China's intelligent computing capacity reached 1.59 million PFLOPS at the end of 2025, ranking second globally. Meanwhile, closer coordination between computing infrastructure and energy supply is channeling more green power to AI development. Barriers that divide the global AI industry risk fragmenting technology ecosystems and undermining international cooperation. Against this backdrop, China's open-source AI models offer the developing world an affordable way to narrow the AI gap and harness the technology to boost productivity. The debate over China's AI industry points to a larger truth about the future of the technology: Progress is rarely linear, and the path forward will inevitably be uneven. Market enthusiasm may fuel its boom, but only continuous innovation and real-world applications can sustain it. China has both the industrial and technological foundation and momentum to carry this progress forward. Ultimately, the industry's trajectory will be shaped not by short-term market swings, but by its ability to exercise patience, keep innovation flowing across borders, and deliver lasting economic value for China and the wider world. item.title: China establishes national sci-tech ethics society to promote responsible innovation
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-28
China establishes national sci-tech ethics society to promote responsible innovation SHANGHAI, Nov. 27 (Xinhua) -- China established a national science and technology ethics society at Fudan University in Shanghai on Friday, bringing together expertise across disciplines to promote responsible innovation and strengthen ethical governance. Mei Hong, the society's first president and an academician of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, said the society will serve as a bridge connecting academic communities in the natural sciences, engineering and technology, and the humanities and social sciences. It aims to promote research cooperation and build a knowledge and practice system for science and technology ethics that is rooted in China and open to the world. The society will also work on ethics norms and standards, provide professional advice, promote education and training, foster academic integrity, and strengthen international exchanges and cooperation, Mei added. The need for stronger ethical governance has grown increasingly pressing as emerging technologies raise complex questions -- from the risks of artificial intelligence to the ethical dilemmas surrounding brain-computer interfaces. The society's establishment follows a 2022 national directive that called for creating a national ethics body to strengthen academic support for ethics governance. "The establishment of the society is an important step in strengthening the organizational system of ethics governance," said Jiang Xiaojuan, a professor at the University of Chinese Academy of Social Sciences. She added that it provides a new platform for integrating academic research with governance practice. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Chinese business community urges U.S. to withdraw proposed tariffs
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-28
Chinese business community urges U.S. to withdraw proposed tariffs BEIJING, Nov. 27 (Xinhua) -- The Chinese business community has urged the United States to withdraw its proposed additional tariffs on China and 13 other economies following a Section 301 investigation into alleged "structural excess capacity" in manufacturing sectors, the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade (CCPIT) said Friday. The Office of the United States Trade Representative recently announced findings of its Section 301 investigation and proposed imposing additional tariffs on 14 economies, including China. "The Chinese business community firmly opposes this," a CCPIT spokesperson said, adding that the community rejects the claim of "structural excess capacity" as a false narrative and opposes the U.S. side using the allegation as a pretext to interfere in normal China-U.S. economic and trade exchanges. Assessments of industrial supply and demand conditions should take into account factors including global market demand, technological progress and investment cycles, the spokesperson said. Trade surpluses are shaped by multiple factors such as the international division of labor, market demand and macroeconomic conditions, and trade surpluses alone are insufficient to determine structural excess capacity. Tariff wars and trade wars benefit no one, the spokesperson said, adding that broad-based tariff hikes will push up procurement costs for U.S. downstream enterprises, place additional burdens on consumers and disrupt global industrial and supply chains. The Chinese business community calls on the United States to withdraw the proposed tariff measures and resolve relevant issues through consultations with China on the basis of equality, respect and mutual benefit, to maintain stable and sound China-U.S. economic and trade relations, the spokesperson said. The CCPIT will continue to follow the concerns of Chinese and U.S. enterprises and foster practical cooperation and communication among the business communities of China, the United States and other countries, the spokesperson added. item.title: China sends key signals to steady capital market
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-28
China sends key signals to steady capital market BEIJING, Nov. 27 (Xinhua) -- A State Council executive meeting on Friday sent key signals from Chinese policymakers on steadying the capital market, with major stock indices surging after the meeting. The meeting, which studied work on further deepening comprehensive investment and financing reforms in the capital market, stressed that the capital market is vital to overall economic development. It called for fully leveraging the existing policies and underscored the need to mull and roll out new measures to promote the steady and sound development of the capital market. More than 5,000 stocks on China's A-share market traded higher on Friday, with a marked increase in the trading volume. The benchmark Shanghai Composite Index closed 3.73 percent higher and the Shenzhen Component Index jumped 7.24 percent. Analysts took note of the meeting's clear positioning of the capital market within the overall framework of economic development, pointing out that the market concerns corporate financing and industrial upgrading as well as household assets and property income. "Stabilizing the stock market means stabilizing expectations, which is of great significance for consolidating the momentum of economic recovery and improvement," said Xie Yaxuan, head of the research and development center at China Merchants Securities. Official data showed that since early October, the amount of share repurchases and shareholding increases implemented by listed companies has reached nearly 60 billion yuan (about 8.9 billion U.S. dollars), far exceeding previous levels. Looking forward, there are greater market expectations for policies to support the capital market and the macroeconomy, analysts said. Friday's meeting emphasized that it is necessary to enhance the role of state-backed funds in stabilizing the market, and optimize the quasi-"stabilization fund" function of the state-owned Central Huijin Investment Ltd. to provide sufficient liquidity. Since early October, net subscriptions of equity exchange-traded funds have reached nearly 800 billion yuan, helping support major stock indices amid market fluctuations. Market observers predicted that the "national team" of state-backed funds will play a more prominent role in the market-stabilization mechanism in the future. The meeting also called for improving policies to support and guide medium- and long-term funds, including insurance funds, enterprise annuity funds and social security funds, to invest in the capital market. Institutional investors have been stepping up countercyclical investment. Publicly offered funds, securities firms' proprietary trading desks, private securities investment funds, social security funds and insurance institutions have all made net purchases of A-shares since early October. The meeting demanded strengthening the capacity to guard against and respond to external risks. This requires taking a coordinated approach to addressing domestic and external risks, said Liu Yu, chief economist at Industrial Securities. Since early October, global technology stocks have experienced sharp fluctuations at elevated levels, with volatility in overseas tech stocks causing a sustained impact on Chinese stocks. China's ChiNext Index, tracking the country's Nasdaq-style board of growth enterprises, has seen its trailing price-to-earnings ratio fall to a historic low. On Friday, the ChiNext Index surged 11.61 percent, while the STAR Composite Index, which reflects the performance of stocks on China's sci-tech innovation board, jumped 14.21 percent. Efforts are expected to strengthen cross-border risk monitoring and early-warning mechanisms as well as policy responses, while drawing on market-stabilization funds and medium- and long-term capital to bolster market resilience and prevent short-term external shocks from triggering sharp market swings, Liu said. item.title: Chinese premier to hold "1+10" dialogue with heads of major international economic organizations
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-28
Chinese premier to hold "1+10" dialogue with heads of major international economic organizations BEIJING, Nov. 27 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang will hold the "1+10" Dialogue in the city of Xiamen, east China's Fujian Province, on the morning of Dec. 2, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson announced on Friday. According to the spokesperson, Li will hold the dialogue with President of the New Development Bank Dilma Rousseff, President of the World Bank Ajay Banga, Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund Kristalina Georgieva, Director-General of the World Trade Organization Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, Acting Secretary-General of the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development Pedro Manuel Moreno, Assistant Director-General of the International Labour Organization Laura Thompson, Secretary-General of the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development Mathias Cormann, General Manager of the Bank for International Settlements Pablo Hernandez de Cos, Chair of the Financial Stability Board Andrew Bailey, and President of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank Zou Jiayi. The spokesperson said that the theme of the dialogue is "Driving Sustained Growth Through Innovation, Promoting Common Development Through Openness." Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. item.title: Beyond the gibbons, China's tropical rainforest regains its rhythm
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-28
Beyond the gibbons, China's tropical rainforest regains its rhythm HAIKOU, Nov. 28 (Xinhua) -- At 4:30 a.m., long before daylight touched Bawangling, a mountainous area of Hainan Tropical Rainforest National Park in south China, Li Wenyong and his fellow wildlife monitors set out with flashlights, threading their way along narrow forest trails. They moved as quietly as possible, knowing that a single unexpected sound could frighten away the Hainan gibbons they had come to track. As dawn broke, the forest came alive with the gibbons' calls. Low, short hoots rose into long, piercing whoops that echoed through the valleys. "Everyone loves the gibbons' songs," Li said. "Protecting the gibbons means protecting the entire rainforest." For decades, those distinctive calls were at risk of disappearing. More than 40 years ago, fewer than 10 Hainan gibbons remained. Today, the population has rebounded to 44 individuals in seven family groups, a turnaround that reflects decades of efforts to protect both these animals and their habitat. Among the world's 20 surviving gibbon species, the Hainan gibbon is the only one with a population that has shown sustained growth, according to local conservation authorities. Hainan Province is home to China's largest, best-preserved and most concentrated stretch of contiguous island tropical rainforest. This forest plays a vital role in conserving water, storing carbon, supporting biodiversity and sustaining local livelihoods. In October 2021, China established Hainan Tropical Rainforest National Park, bringing more than 20 previously separate nature reserves and forest parks under unified management. Covering over 4,269 square kilometers, the park hosts 4,367 recorded species of higher plants and 651 vertebrate species. It is one of China's first five national parks, which together protect some of the country's most important ecosystems, including giant panda habitats in Sichuan, Gansu and Shaanxi provinces and tiger and leopard habitats in northeast China. China has also implemented its national park law and revised regulations on nature reserves, marking a new stage of law-based and standardized development for its nature reserve system with national parks as the main body. In Hainan, conservation efforts have focused on restoring habitats, creating ecological corridors to connect fragmented forest areas, strengthening wildlife monitoring, and involving local communities in conservation. "The rainforest ecosystem is gradually finding its natural rhythm again," said Chen Kang, director of the Hainan Tropical Rainforest National Park Administration. More than 90 new species have been discovered in Hainan's tropical rainforest in recent years, noted Zhou Runbang, an official with the provincial forestry department. Fan Pengfei, a professor at Sun Yat-sen University, said efforts to protect flagship species and their habitats have helped restore the wider ecosystem, taking conservation in Hainan beyond individual species to the forest as a whole. The benefits of rainforest conservation, notably, extend beyond wildlife to local communities. Over the past five years, the national park in Hainan has recruited 1,593 local residents as full-time ecological rangers, while ecological compensation has benefited 372 village collectives and 6,194 rural households. The park's gross ecosystem product (GEP), a measure of the economic value of ecosystem services, reached 208.97 billion yuan (around 31.15 billion U.S. dollars) in 2024, according to a think-tank report. Ecotourism is growing, supported by a 466-kilometer scenic highway linking attractions and villages of the Li and Miao ethnic groups across nine cities and counties in Hainan. Hainan is also seeking UNESCO World Heritage status for its tropical rainforest and the traditional settlement of the Li ethnic group, which have been jointly added to the World Heritage tentative list. Speaking at the 2026 Tropical Rainforest Ecosystem Partners Conference recently held in Haikou, capital of Hainan, Carlos Aldeco, the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations representative in China, described Hainan as an example of how nature conservation and sustainable development can go hand in hand. He highlighted the province's efforts to protect biodiversity while creating opportunities for environmental education, sustainable livelihoods and responsible ecotourism. As climate change intensifies and extreme weather events become more frequent, tropical rainforests face growing risks of habitat degradation and biodiversity loss. Paul Shrivastava, co-president of the Club of Rome, said China's concept of ecological civilization encourages people to live sustainably within ecosystems rather than simply extracting resources from nature. Shrivastava commended China for being at the forefront of such efforts, saying its actions could help drive positive change around the world. But protecting tropical rainforests also requires cooperation across borders. Zhang Xinsheng, former president of the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), said no country or organization can protect tropical rainforests in isolation, calling for closer collaboration across countries, sectors and scientific disciplines to share knowledge and address common threats. The IUCN has introduced this experience to the international community as an example of "Chinese wisdom, Hainan experience and the Bawangling Model." Hainan has also led the establishment of the Global Gibbon Network, with its secretariat located at the Hainan Institute of National Park, bringing together 36 conservation institutions from 11 countries to jointly carry out gibbon conservation research. Back in Bawangling, the results of conservation are visible in the footage collected by Li and his fellow wildlife monitors. Their videos now regularly show gibbons swinging along ropes installed to help them cross gaps in the forest canopy, while each morning, their calls continue to echo through the valleys. "I hope I can keep hearing them forever," Li said. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.
